answer: Proposed bridge commits each key to a Merkle root of a 64-GiB key-salted memory-hard state. A falcon audit probes 32 random offsets on all keys in one unpredictable ripple window; validators check proofs against roots before deadline. A farm can share a model and rent machines, but each clone needs its own resident state: one salt’s bytes cannot serve another. Each also locks a distinct 30-epoch bond; a missed deadline or false proof burns it. Renting or borrowing still ties up one RAM lease and bond per clone. If either is skipped, validators pay zero. MinePoA does not enforce this proposal.
